Claim: PM loop round 38 (refill slot)
Session: `session_01CSoz9uGhaaSgiq3hshtN7L`
Branch: `claude/issue-5969-activity-feed-open-vocabulary-pin`
Worktree: `objectui-issue-5969`
Domain: `domain:ui`
File surface: `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/recordActivityFeed.ts` and its tests, plus a changeset if one is owed. ⛔ Nothing else.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus`
Clause-②: **no** — a pin plus, at most, a defined fallback presentation. No published declaration moves.
⚠️ **Serial:** **#6088 is enqueued** and touches `packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/` — a different file, but branch from a base containing it once it lands. Other siblings in flight: #5828 (`app-shell/src/console/__tests__/`), #5729 (`packages/plugin-grid`), #5852 (`packages/types`, dashboard config), #5861 (`packages/types/src/objectql.ts` + `packages/plugin-view`). ⛔ Do not touch `plugin-view` or `packages/types`.

## 裁决 — the maintainer ruling, already made

Maintainer, 2026-08-24, batch acceptance on objectstack#11507, verbatim: 「四维分析一致的，接手你的建议。」 — adopting the aligned four-facet recommendation, **direction 4: `sys_activity.type` is author-extensible**.

⛔ The vocabulary question is **settled**. Do not re-open it, and ⛔ do not restore set-equality.

## What this card does — both halves, or neither

In `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/recordActivityFeed.ts`:

1. **Pin the open-vocabulary contract, in two directions:**
   - **Superset assertion** — the feed-kind map covers the platform's **built-in** set, measured against the declared options, so a **new built-in turns the pin red** and the map is forced to keep up.
   - **Fallback assertion** — an **unknown / author-extended `type` renders through a defined fallback presentation**: ⛔ never dropped, ⛔ never crashing.
   ⚠️ Both halves, or neither. A superset pin alone re-creates the closed-vocabulary failure in slow motion; a fallback pin alone lets the map silently fall behind the platform.
2. **The pin's docblock names the ruling** — objectstack#11507, direction 4, 2026-08-24 — ⚠️ **so the next sweep does not "restore" set-equality.** That sentence is load-bearing: #5840 removed the old set-equality pin deliberately, and without the citation the next reader sees a missing equality check and helpfully puts it back.

## ⛔ Boundary

This card does **not** touch the platform declaration. Making the select declaration honest about open semantics is the services-lane half and rides objectstack#11507 itself. ✅ No coordination is needed: the fallback-rendering pin is correct under the ruled semantics **regardless of when the declaration lands**. ⛔ If you find yourself wanting to edit anything outside `plugin-detail`, stop and report.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not inherit

1. ⚠️ **"The platform's built-in set" has to come from somewhere real.** Establish where the declared options actually live — the installed `@objectstack/spec`, a served schema, or a local mirror — and read them from **that**, ⛔ not from a list you retype into the test. A pin that compares the map against a copy of itself is a phantom: it stays green when the platform adds a built-in, which is the exact event it exists to catch. ✅ Say in your report which source you read and how you proved it is the live one.
2. ⚠️ **The superset direction is easy to get backwards.** *Map ⊇ built-ins* is the assertion (every built-in has a presentation). *Built-ins ⊇ map* is a **different** claim and is false by construction under direction 4, since author-extended values legitimately exist outside the declaration. ⛔ Do not assert set equality in either spelling. ✅ State the direction you asserted in words as well as in code.
3. ⚠️ **A "renders through a fallback" assertion is trivially satisfiable by rendering nothing.** The fallback leg needs a **positive** observable — the row is present, and it is distinguishable from a known built-in's presentation — plus its counter-probe in the same run: a **known built-in** still renders its own presentation, ⛔ not the fallback. Without that, "unknown types do not crash" is also true of a feed that drops every row.
4. ⚠️ **Check whether a defined fallback already exists before writing one.** The card says *"renders through a defined fallback presentation"*, which may be describing existing behaviour to be pinned rather than behaviour to be added. ⚠️ Adjacent and unresolved: **#5891** records that `record:activity`'s `filterMode` sanitiser folds every unrecognised value onto `all` — the widest option, silently — and **#5896** records that the console surface **drops unmapped types silently**. ⛔ If what you find is a silent drop rather than a defined fallback, then this card is a **behaviour change**, not just a pin: say so explicitly, keep it minimal, and name it in the changeset.
5. ⚠️ **#5840 is the direct precedent — read what it removed and why** before writing the replacement. It broke the old set-equality pin because pinning to the closed declaration meant **dropping stored rows**. ✅ Your new pin must not be able to re-create that outcome.

## Verification

Predict the direction **before** running. ⚠️ **Commit your own edit before you ablate** — measured on #5859 today: a `trap` restore using `git checkout --` reverted the dev's still-uncommitted edit along with the probe's mutation, and `git checkout --` **reported success both times**; the half-change was caught only by an independent `git diff --stat` re-read.

⚠️ **Two phantom-pin failures were caught by devs on this round's own cards** — one assertion that was green against both the fixed and the unfixed source, and one whose *control* line failed, making a real revert and a broken probe indistinguishable. So: ✅ state, explicitly, **which of your assertions would still pass if your change were reverted**, and re-aim or delete any that would; and ✅ make each control a string present in **both** versions of the file.

Ablate each half separately — remove a built-in's entry and show the superset leg goes red; remove the fallback and show the fallback leg goes red — with the other leg staying green each time, and the greens predicted too. Prove every mutation on disk by grepping injected **and separately** removed text; ⚠️ print the landing site; ⚠️ assert anchor uniqueness before writing; ⚠️ restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with a **cwd-independent** command; confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` is empty afterwards.

**Gates by name, with exit codes:** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail type-check` (⚠️ hyphenated; echo the script name; distinguish the **unbuilt-closure** red — `Cannot find module @object-ui/...` — from the **missing-`node_modules`** red; a fresh worktree needs its dependency closure built, and ⚠️ **build `./examples/**` too** — that exact gap turned a sweep red on #5876 today and was environmental, not a finding), root-form vitest over `packages/plugin-detail/src` quoting per-test names, the downstream **prefix-form** sweep with the direction **demonstrated** (say how many packages it matches) rather than asserted, and eslint with merge-base delta (⚠️ plain `eslint .`; ⛔ no `--no-inline-config`).

⚠️ **Use `pnpm exec vitest run [paths]` from the repo root** — ⛔ **not** `pnpm --filter … test -- [paths]`, which **silently drops everything after `--`** and runs the whole default set. This repo has a guard for it (objectui#3288) and it fired on a live PR today.

Run `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` rather than guessing — ⚠️ **#6073 landed today and widened that gate's notion of a package's source** beyond `/src/`; a test-only change usually owes nothing, and empty frontmatter is this repo's explicit "releases nothing" declaration. If item 4 turns this into a behaviour change, it owes a real `patch`.

⚠️ **Standing rule from #5874:** derive your gate set by enumerating **each CI job's own step list**, ⛔ not from top-level script names — `check:esm-specifiers` runs as a step inside the `Type Check` job under a name that does not read like one, and that class of miss turned a PR red today.

## Deliverable

Draft PR, body with `Fixes #5969`. ⛔ Do not mark ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ no auto-merge — the PM lands it. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — this repo's sanitizer eats them, confirmed three times today) and return it. State, per gate: command, exit code, what a red would have meant; where you read the built-in set from and how you proved it live; the direction you asserted, in words; whether item 4 made this a behaviour change; **which of your assertions would still pass on a revert**; and any deviation with its reason.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**, enqueued. And **assumption 1 was wrong in the most useful way.**

PR **#6112** at `8740317bc`. Gates read **once** at 18:00:30Z, off this run's own `started_at` (17:46:37Z). **22 checks, 19 success + 3 skipped, 0 failing, 0 still running.** Marked ready and enqueued; ⛔ nothing merged by hand.

### My assumption 1 does not hold here — and proving that is the card's most valuable output

I wrote: *read the built-in set from a live source, ⛔ not a list you retype into the test, or the pin compares the map against a copy of itself.* ✅ Correct as a principle, ⛔ **impossible as an instruction here**, and the dev measured why rather than quietly retyping:

`sys_activity.type` is declared **only** in `@objectstack/plugin-audit` — a **server** plugin. objectui depends on `@objectstack/spec`, `client`, `formula` and `lint`; the spec publishes `FeedItemType` (the map's **values**) and **never its keys**, and `@objectstack/platform-objects` does not carry it either (its `src/audit/index.ts` records the move to plugin-audit under ADR-0029 K2). Reading it live would mean **a UI package depending on a services plugin** — outside this card's boundary and arguably outside any UI card's.

⇒ So the census is a **documented hand copy** — ⚠️ **and it had already drifted, measured in the act**: `scheduled` was declared upstream by objectstack#11522 **on 2026-08-24**, while the previous census still filed it as *"undeclared but written"*. That is exactly the phantom I described, caught on the same day it appeared.

✅ Read from the declaration at objectstack `91b1342`, 12 options, and proved it is the **only** declaration by grepping every spelling of the vocabulary across objectstack `packages/` and `apps/` — one non-test hit. ✅ Filed **objectstack#11807** to publish the built-in set where a UI consumer can read it **without re-closing the vocabulary**. Until that lands, the fallback is what keeps this drift costing **an icon rather than a row**.

### Item 4: **yes, a behaviour change** — and bigger than the card said

What existed was a **drop, not a fallback**: `activityRowToFeedItem` returned `null` for any `sys_activity.type` outside the map, so an author-extended value was **stored, queryable, and invisible**. That is #5840's failure reached by another route, and #5896 had recorded the console half of it. ✅ Correctly identified as a behaviour change, declared in a real `patch` changeset, ⛔ not smuggled in as "just a pin".

✅ The four deliberate exclusions (`commented` / `mentioned` / `login` / `logout`) still return `null` **silently**, and `ACTIVITY_TYPE_TO_FEED_TYPE` itself is untouched, so `RecordDetailView`'s consumer is unaffected.

### The direction was stated in words, and the converse was pinned as false

> *map ⊇ built-ins — every value the platform DECLARES has an entry in the map (a feed type, or an explicit `undefined` exclusion); the converse is NOT asserted, and set equality is not asserted in either spelling.*

⭐ And a **second test asserts the non-containment positively**, so **restoring equality now requires deleting a passing test**. That is a materially better guard than a comment — it is the mechanism that stops #5840's removal from being "helpfully" undone, which is precisely what the ruling citation in the docblock exists to prevent and what a future sweep would otherwise do.

### The revert answer was given honestly, including the uncomfortable half

> *The superset leg and the whole-table regression control stay **GREEN** on a revert; the four fallback-dependent tests go **RED**.*

✅ And the reason is stated rather than hidden: the superset leg pins a **map/platform relation that already holds today** — it is not a test of this behaviour change, and its discriminating power is measured separately by ablating the **map** (ablation A). Both ablations behaved exactly as predicted: (A) delete `assigned: 'field_change'` → superset red naming `assigned`, fallback green; (B) point the unknown branch back at `undefined` → 4 fallback tests red, superset and table control green. ✅ Two ablations, disjoint red sets, each leg's greens predicted too.

### The open question: **A stands — leave the fallback at `system`**

The dev asks whether an unmapped row should be visually distinct from a genuine platform `system` row. ✅ **A, as shipped**, and the reasoning is right on the axis that matters here: `FeedItemType` is a **spec-owned closed enum**, and a UI package ⛔ must not mint into it. B is the contract-first route if this is ever wanted, and it belongs on the services lane with objectstack#11507 — ⛔ not here. C needs `packages/types`, which this card was forbidden to touch.

⚠️ And the measured need was never "tell an extended row from a system row" — it was **"extended rows exist at all and were invisible"**. That need is now met. The console diagnostic names the exact value and the exact map to add it to, which for an authoring agent is a stronger correction signal than a different icon. ⛔ Not escalating this one; it is a cosmetic question with no measured demand behind it. Revisit if a real app reports confusing the two.

### Second open question — handled as a PM action, correctly

✅ The dev did **not** edit `app-shell` (the boundary forbade it, `ACTIVITY_TYPE_TO_FEED_TYPE` is untouched, nothing regressed) and instead flagged that #5896 and #5878 are now inconsistent with this card. **Done:** #5896 carries an annotation naming objectstack#11507 direction 4, the four exclusions that must stay excluded, and the hand-copy trap. Whoever takes it will not have to rediscover any of it.

### Two gate readings worth keeping

⚠️ **Environmental red, resolved, correctly not filed:** app-shell `type-check` first exited 2 with `Cannot find module '@object-ui/auth' / plugin-chatbot / plugin-view / plugin-list / plugin-form` — the **unbuilt-closure** signature, **with no `@object-ui/plugin-detail` among them**, which is the detail that identifies it. Green after building the closure.

✅ **Declared narrowing with evidence:** the downstream test sweep ran `packages/app-shell/src/views` rather than all 11 dependents, because grep showed app-shell is the **only** downstream package referencing the changed module's exports (2 files; the other 9 match zero). ⛔ A narrowing asserted would be a gap; a narrowing measured is a decision.

Direction demonstrated, not asserted: prefix form matches **11** (consumers), suffix form **13** (dependencies).

Cross-repo coupling note from the spec lane (objectstack-ai/objectstack#11658, PR objectstack-ai/objectstack#12408, draft): the authoring surface this card's feed-kind map consumes has widened. `RecordActivityProps.types` (also `RecordChatterProps.feed.types`) is no longer a closed `z.array(FeedItemType)` — its element is now `z.union([FeedItemType, z.string().min(1)])`, so an authored `types` entry can name ANY non-empty string: built-in feed kinds remain autocomplete/JSON-Schema `anyOf` guidance, and author-contributed activity kinds (open `sys_activity.type` vocabulary, #11507 direction-4 ruling; e.g. `scheduled`) are equally legal and are never validated against the built-in set.

Consequence for the map this card pins: the renderer can now receive filter entries outside `FeedItemType` and must treat them as first-class kinds to match against (not silently drop the filter entry, and not fold unknown source types into a built-in kind the filter can no longer separate). No objectui code changed by that PR — this is a note only, per the card's cross-repo read-coupling instruction.
